title: "04_describe"
format: html

## Load libraries and data

```{r}
library("here")
library("tidyverse")

dat_aug <- read_tsv(here("data/03_augmented_data.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Give the outcome groups descriptive names and set the order of the class columns again:

```{r}
dat_aug <- dat_aug |>
  mutate(
    progression_status = factor(
      progression_status,
      levels = c("Persistent","Regressive", "Progressive", "Stable non-dysplasia")
    ),
    smoking_exposure = factor(
      smoking_exposure,
      levels = c("Never smoker", "Light smoker", "Moderate smoker", "Heavy smoker")
    ),
  )
```

## 1. Histological transition: baseline → follow-up

Bigger points mean more biopsies. Grades 4–7 are dysplasia, so the dashed line separates dysplastic (above) from nondysplastic (below) follow-up biopsies.

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  count(progression_status, baseline_frozen, followup) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = baseline_frozen, y = followup, colour = progression_status)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Histological grade: baseline vs follow-up",
    x = "Baseline grade",
    y = "Follow-up grade",
    colour = NULL,
    size = "Biopsies"
  )
```

## 2. Age distribution

```{r}
ggplot(dat_aug, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "cadetblue3") +
  labs(
    title = "Age distribution",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

## 3. Are age and smoking related?

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  summarise(correlation = cor(age, smoking_pack_years))
```

```{r}
ggplot(dat_aug, aes(x = age, y = smoking_pack_years)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = smoking_exposure)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Older patients have smoked more pack-years",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Pack-years",
    colour = NULL
  )
```

## 4. Is smoking balanced across the outcome groups?

```{r}
ggplot(dat_aug, aes(x = progression_status, fill = smoking_exposure)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Smoking class within each outcome group", x = NULL, y = "Count", fill = NULL)
```

## 5. PCA

Gene columns are named by Entrez ID (a number), so `matches("^[0-9]")` selects all genes.

```{r}
pca <- dat_aug |>
  dplyr::select(matches("^[0-9]")) |>
  prcomp(scale. = TRUE)

pca_data <- bind_cols(
  dat_aug |> dplyr::select(progression_status, baseline_frozen),
  pca |> pluck("x") |> as_tibble()
)

# Does PC2 follow the histological grade?
pca_data |>
  summarise(correlation = cor(PC2, baseline_frozen))
```

```{r}
ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = progression_status)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "PCA of all genes", colour = NULL)
```

## 6. Marker genes by outcome group

**MKI67** and **TOP2A**: cell division. **KRT6A**: squamous cells (dysplasia). **FOXJ1**: ciliated cells (normal airway).

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  dplyr::select(progression_status, MKI67 = "4288", TOP2A = "7153", FOXJ1 = "2302", KRT6A = "3853") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -progression_status, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expression") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gene, y = expression, fill = progression_status)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Marker genes by outcome group", x = NULL, y = "log2 expression", fill = NULL)
```

## 7. Smoking-related genes by smoking class

**CYP1B1**: switched on by cigarette smoke. **SCGB1A1**: made by protective club cells, which are lost in smokers.

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  dplyr::select(smoking_exposure, CYP1B1 = "1545", SCGB1A1 = "7356") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -smoking_exposure, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expression") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gene, y = expression, fill = smoking_exposure)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Smoking-related genes by smoking class", x = NULL, y = "log2 expression", fill = NULL)
```

## Observations

1.  **Histology:** persistent and progressive biopsies are dysplastic at follow-up; regressive and stable normal are not. Regressive and progressive biopsies change by several grades.
2.  **Age classes:** Younger < 55.5 (16), Middle-aged 55.5–65 (32), Older > 65 (15).
3.  **Age and smoking are correlated** (r ≈ 0.45), so they should not be treated as independent predictors.
4.  **Smoking:** most samples are heavy smokers and only 2 are never-smokers, but the mix is similar in every outcome group, so smoking is unlikely to explain group differences.
5.  **PCA:** the groups separate along PC2, which follows histological grade (r ≈ 0.6). Much of the variation in gene expression reflects how dysplastic the tissue is.
6.  **Marker genes:** MKI67, TOP2A and KRT6A are highest in persistent dysplasia and lowest in stable normal; FOXJ1 shows the opposite. Dysplastic tissue divides more and loses normal airway cells.
7.  **Smoking genes:** CYP1B1 rises and SCGB1A1 falls with heavier smoking, but the spread within each class is large.
